props.title: Room for Error
lines: The most important part of every plan is planning on the plan not going according to plan.
Room for error is the only way an uncertain world stays survivable.

props.title: Avoid ruin even when the odds look good

rows.v: U.S. stocks: annual average about 6.8% after inflation since the 1870s — with brutal variation around that mean.
Infrastructure projects often run 25% to 50% over budget. Your life plan will too.
You can be risk-loving and still averse to ruin. Russian roulette has favorable odds. The downside is still unacceptable.
If something is 95% likely, the 5% will still happen in a long life. If that 5% is ruin, do not take the bet.
Use a gap between what can happen and what you need to happen. That gap is the room for error.

props.title: The mean is not the life you live

rows.v: About 6.8% a year after inflation since the 1870s — an average that hides years that feel like ruin.
Projects run 25% to 50% over budget. Your retirement math should assume the same slop.
A 95% bet will still hit the 5% in a long life. If the 5% is bankruptcy, the bet is illegal for you.
Risk-loving and ruin-averse can coexist. That is the adult version of room for error.

props.title: Leave slack on purpose
items: Save more than the model. Spend less than the peak year. Borrow less than the bank offers.
A plan that only works if every assumption is right is not a plan. It is a wish.
